title: Two-Step Relaxation in a Linear Tetranuclear Dysprosium(III) Aggregate Showing Single-Molecule Magnet Behavior

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: [Dy4(L)4(MeOH)6]·2MeOH (L = trianion of 2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzoic acid [(2-hydroxy-3-methoxyphenyl)methylene]hydrazide); crystallographic/elemental formula corresponds to C74H92Dy4N8O30, i.e. four methanol solvate molecules

synthesis.procedure: H3L was prepared first: methyl 2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzoate (1.82 g, 10 mmol) and hydrazine hydrate (85%, 15 mL) in methanol (20 mL) were refluxed for 5 h somewhat below 40 °C, neutralized with concentrated HCl, stirred 15 min, and left overnight to give 2-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzoic acid hydrazide (0.96 g, 53%). That hydrazide (1 mmol, 0.182 g) and o-vanillin (1 mmol, 0.152 g) in methanol (10 mL) were stirred at room temperature overnight; the pale-yellow H3L was filtered and washed with ether (0.27 g, 85%). Compound 1: a suspension of DyCl3·6H2O (0.2 mmol, 75.4 mg) and H3L (0.2 mmol, 63.2 mg) in MeOH/MeCN (5 mL/20 mL) was treated with Et3N (1.0 mmol, 0.14 mL). The yellow solution was stirred for 6 h, filtered, and the filtrate left for slow evaporation. Yellow crystals of [Dy4(L)4(MeOH)6]·2MeOH formed after 2 days. Yield 38 mg (34% based on the metal salt). The main text only states that DyCl3·6H2O and H3L in 1:4 methanol/acetonitrile with triethylamine give pale-yellow crystals, without numerical reagent amounts.
synthesis.temperature: complexation temperature not stated; H3L precursors: reflux somewhat below 40 °C, then room temperature overnight

properties.summary: Homometallic Dy4 single-molecule magnet with two distinct relaxation processes under zero dc field. χMT falls from 54.9 cm3 K mol−1 at 300 K to 31.3 cm3 K mol−1 at 2 K. Out-of-phase ac susceptibility shows two peaks (about 1.2 and 1200 Hz at 7 K). Arrhenius analysis gives Ueff = 19.7 K (fast) and 173 K (slow), with τ0 = 7.8×10−6 s and 1.2×10−7 s. The fast process crosses from Orbach to a direct/phonon-induced tunneling regime below about 6 K; the slow process between 7 and 18 K follows a Raman law (1/τ2 ∝ T^5). Cole–Cole plots at 7 and 8 K fit the sum of two modified Debye functions. No magnetic hysteresis is observed above 1.9 K at conventional SQUID sweep rates. No optical properties are reported.
